chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: The tuba ensemble at the party
summary: He and Carl Fontana did not play together; a tuba ensemble played Basie arrangements.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Now, last year at the party, Carl and I didn't play together at all, Carl Fontana.
Not on all those days? Really?
Those three days, we didn't get a chance to play together at all.
That's strange.
And --
So he went on mixing it up just as much as ever, last year, too, huh?
Well, yes, he mixed it up just as much as ever last year. Last year he had all tubas playing.
For heaven's sake.
But you should have been there to hear it.
I'll bet that was something to hear.
It was beautiful.
Was it?
I mean, they played a bass in --
Well, who was playing? Was Red Cal-lender playing tuba?
No, no, no. That's --
Oh, you mean the tuba group -- the 17 tubas.
Yes, a group.
Oh.
And they played an arrangement of one of Basie's numbers, and they just swung that place --
Well, who are they? (Rich Matteson-Harvey Phillips Tubajazz--ed.)
I don't know them. I don't know them myself. This is the first time I --
They're black guys?
No, white guys.
No kidding. What age, around?
They range --
Middle-30's or something?
Or something. 30's, 40's.
It was a kind of nostalgia thing, too?
Yes, yes. And Ray Brown's wife was there. And I said, 'I wonder what's the surprise group this time?' See, the year before that, it was the Japanese girls.
Yeah, yeah.
And so she said, 'Oh, a bunch of tubas.' And so I figured she was putting me on, because I'm always kidding with her, and Ray Brown, you see.
Yes.
And I said, 'Oh, get out of here.' She said, 'A bunch of tubas.' I say, 'Yeah? How do they sound?' Like a bunch of tubas, she said. And I just knew she was putting me on.
Yeah, sure.
So the next day, I was coming back over to the hall where we were playing, the auditorium, and I happened to see a party, and I said, 'Who's on there?' And so they

said, 'the tuba players are on.' I said, 'the tuba players?' They said, 'yeah.' I said, 'Oh, yeah, that's right, they do have tuba players.' I didn't believe them, I just said it. And went inside, and they had just finished playing one number. They started on that next number, the Basie number, and they sounded beautiful, just like a --
So they could score it for that many parts?
Right, right, right.
Is that right?
They certainly did.
And it could move that fast, to play a Basie arrangement?
You would be surprised.
I would be surprised.
It shocked me, you know. And they were wonderful. I wish I could think of their names.
What kind of a drummer did they have?
Good drummer, they had a good drummer. He just kept good time, one of those things. No flashy stuff. But he played good with them.
Fancy that. Isn't that an amazing thing?
It was wonderful.
Well, anyway, Dick didn't mix them up. He left them --
Oh, no, no, everything was all right.
